learning_outcomes.text: He is able to define basic quantities in Mechanics (Force and momentum). He knows conditions of static equilibrium of forces system.

He knows the Centroid of Area, the center of Gravity of a Mass, Moments of inertia, Product of inertia, Parallel–axis theorem, Rotation transformation of Moments of inertia, Inertia Tensor, inertia ellipsoid, the principal axes.

He is able to define key concepts in Kinematics, motion of particle, trajectory, one–dimensional model. Velocity and acceleration in natural coordinates. Rigid body, The Degrees of Freedom, Classification of motions, Velocity and acceleration in general motion.
He can solve typical engineering structures (Trusses, Beams & Frames) under statical loading. Conditions of static equilibrium of forces system. Plane forces system reduction.

He can calculate the Centroid of Area, the center of Gravity of a Mass, Moments of inertia, Product of inertia, He can use Parallel–axis theorem, Rotation transformation of Moments of inertia, Inertia Tensor, inertia ellipsoid, the principal axes.

He can calculate the velocity and acceleration in plane motion of a rigid body and in the relative motion of a point. He can derive the equations of motion of a free and constrained material point for time-varying dynamic loads using the Newton's second principle.
He can search information and is able to review it critically.
He can objectively evaluate the arguments as well as rationally explain and justify the own point of view.
He can observe customs and rules of academic community

syllabus_topics: Curriculum. Requirements. Literature.Theory of vectors algebra
Force and momentum. Principal vector and principal momentum of forces system. Statics. Conditions of static equilibrium of forces system. The change of momentum point.
Concurrent forces system.Trusses. Method of Joints.
Plane forces system. Reactions in the statically determinate systems (Beams, Trusses, Frames).
Conditions of static equilibrium of forces system. Plane forces system reduction.
Internal forces in Beams (analytical methods, diagrams).
Internal forces in Frames (analytical methods, diagrams).
Centroid of Area. The center of Gravity of a Mass.
Moments of inertia. Product of inertia. Parallel–axis theorem. Rotation transformation of Moments of inertia,
Inertia tensor, inertia ellipsoid. The principal axes.
Kinematics, motion of particle, trajectory, one–dimensional model. Velocity, acceleration. Velocity and acceleration in natural coordinates.
Rigid body, The Degrees of Freedom, Classification of motions, Velocity and acceleration in general motion.
Plane motion and rotation over permanent axis. Planar motion of rigid body, velocity, center of circulation.
Centroids, acceleration in a planar motion of rigid body.
Relative motion. Kinematics in a general motion of rigid body. The Coriolis' acceleration.
Vectors algebra
Trusses. Method of Joints. Analytical methods of trusses solving.
Reactions in the statically determinate plane systems. Analytical methods.
Reactions in the statically determinate space systems. Analytical methods.
Analytical methods of trusses solving. The Ritter’s methods.
Test 1: Vectors, Trusses
Internal forces in beams (analytical methods, diagrams).
Internal forces in beams (analytical methods, diagrams). Beams with Joints.
Internal forces in Frames (analytical methods, diagrams).
Test 1: Internal forces in plane structures
Centroid of Area. The center of Gravity of discrete Multi-mass structures.
Centroid of Area. The center of Gravity of continue-mass structures.
Moments of inertia & inertia products. Parallel–axis theorem.
Rotation transformation of Moments of inertia, inertia tensor, inertia ellipsoid. Principal axes.
Test 3: The center of Gravity of a Mass. Moments of inertia.
Kinematics of particle in orthogonal coordinates.
Kinematics of rigid body. Plane motion and rotation over permanent axis.
Velocity in a plane motion.
Test 4: Kinematics (task by yourself choose.)
teaching_methods: Traditional lecture with the use of transparencies and slides
Four small tests instead of two big make students more regular in the study
assessment_rules: The lecture is evaluated by an oral-writing exam. For classes, P = 2 if F1=2. If not, P=(2F1+F2+F3)/4.
